decision: Yes: loops are ordinary versions. The ABC loop subsystem retires, and the driver's key rule becomes concrete: a plain forward edge keeps constants; an edge into a function-entry pc joins that entry's lattice-keyed version (per continuation for virtual entries); an edge into a non-entry loop header uses the generic all-location key; the budget fallback uses the same generic key. Loop headers join shared module facts (a leader with an incoming edge whose source pc >= it), replacing the C sink's private scan; the C sink's per-slot recursion widening and native's backward-edge constant weakening collapse into that one rule. The key is corrected to constants + binding locations + the continuation chain. The ABC location vocabulary is justified rather than asserted: verifier-fixed join shapes make the target layout a function of the target pc, and because the body is emitted once for many predecessors while the emitter can only address the C frame, A/B values are drained into C slots at the edge (rejected alternative: key A/B positions and read them in place). Q8 answered; Q9 opened as a narrow native version-policy gate (native currently peels one iteration by keeping constants on a forward loop-header edge); Q1's case now includes the measured local-loop coverage cliff; ARCHITECTURE.md, LOG.md and QUESTIONS.md updated.

decision: The lattice is a module-level fixpoint over residual functions whose widening discards and rebuilds the entire function buffer — and it should not be built. ARCHITECTURE now makes a key exact and never widened; the only forced-generic triggers are (i) a residual-call entry, because a call that can only name a function entry must be correct for every caller, and (ii) the per-pc version budget. A residual function has exactly one generic-key entry version; there is no join, no call facts, no re-execution, no rebuild, and the module-wide invariant "each version body is executed exactly once" is restored. Specialization across calls comes from inlining: a direct call becomes a virtual entry — an ordinary version carrying the caller's constants and its continuation chain — bounded by a new per-residual-function version budget, with a residual call (generic entry) as the fallback; nontail recursive cycles must stay residual because inlining grows the continuation chain that is part of key identity. The ABC argument-fact machinery (ArgumentFact, record_call facts, activate/join_call_facts, the dirty loop), the dead residual_analysis lattice and the builder's argument_facts hook join the retired-path list, and the documented docs/abc-opt.md:25,100 behavior removal rides on Q1's gate. Q7 is revised to this answer; Q10 (ABC inline rule and its bound) and Q11 (loop-header key form: generic vs per-slot join vs exact-key unrolling) are opened; Q9's uniform-generic recommendation is weakened by the measured invariant-constant loss; Q1/Q4/Q5 are refined. The lattice alternative stays on record with its measured mechanism and cost as the fallback if cross-call constants are required.
next: Q11 is now the last place where a key is deliberately generalized while constants are still available: deciding whether "no widening anywhere except the forced entry plus the budget" is the whole key rule requires knowing the version count and code size of exact-key loop headers (a constant-initialized changing slot unrolls up to the per-pc budget and then converges to the generic version) versus one body with a loop-granular widening join. That needs a versioned-driver prototype over the optimizer corpus after Q10 fixes the ABC inline rule and its budget, and Q2 still blocks a single budget number.

question: Under round 4's "keys are exact; generalize only at a residual-call entry or the per-pc budget", what key must an edge into a non-entry loop header take — exact keys (unroll to the budget), the round-3 generic all-location key, or the per-slot join — and can that key be computed without restoring the widening fixpoint/rebuild round 4 deleted? (Ranked above the per-version drain/entry-layout contract, fixed by round 3's fixtures, and above where per-pc layouts/may-write sets live, opened as Q12.)
evidence: experiments/5-loop-key.md §1 and experiments/5-loop-key.lua: the incumbent's optimized documented counter (frontend/tests/optimize.lua:229) is ONE loop body at pc 6 — `CGET0_A; BLTUI_A 50` with body `CGET0_A; ADDI_A 7; ZX32_A; CGET1_A; ADDI_A 1; ZX32_A; CSETN_A 1; CSET0_A; JMP 6` — both loop-carried slots unknown while bound 50 and step 7 stay constants in the same body, and frontend/tests/optimize.lua:502,505 pins those immediates. So the documented loop header is a join that widens written slots and keeps unwritten constants.

experiments/5-loop-key.md §2 (measured, artifacts experiments/5-loop-key-out/, all return 1071 in interpreted/threaded/compiled/lazy): loop-invariant-key emission P = 16 instructions, one body, 10 instructions/iteration, `BLTUI_A 120` + `ADDI_A 7`; generic-key emission G = 22 instructions, 12/iteration, bound/step are `CGETN_B` reads; exact-key emission E with budget 8 = 29 instructions (seven folded header versions that are single jumps, four constant stores at the budget edge, then an all-location tail at 12/iteration with no immediates). Computed executed-instruction counts at trip 18: 188 / 229 / 152; exact keys win only for small constant trip counts (break-even about 36 iterations).

experiments/5-loop-key-out/G-generic.c and src/residual_builder.c:1090-1091, 1195-1207: the shipped portable-C sink materializes the bound before the loop but its loop-entry version compares block-argument copies `if(v_8 < v_5)` because `edge_version_mode` forgets constants at a loop entry; src/residualize.c:414-438 weakens all constants on a native backward edge, giving two header versions and reading an invariant C-frame bound.

Derivation (§3): a key component can differ between iterations only if the loop changes or destroys its storage, so the join's fixpoint is the entry key with the may-write components widened; that set is static (ABC: loop-interval CSET/CPUSH writes, minimum A/B/C heights, call argument bases; native: the same over A/B depths and C-frame homes), so the loop-invariant key is available when the version is created — no fixpoint, no re-execution, no rebuild, no call facts, and one version per single-entry loop header.

Consequences: a self-tail call inlines as a loop header whose backedge canonicalizes to the loop-invariant key (one-version cycle), which derives the incumbent's self-recursive inline rule (optimize.c:301,309-318) and leaves Q10's inline budget to bound only nontail chains (continuation chains in key identity, src/symbolic.c:39-75).
decision: Q11 is answered: a non-entry loop header's key is the static loop-invariant key, applied as a canonicalization to every edge into the header (every component whose storage the loop may write or destroy becomes the binding's location form; every other component keeps its constant). Exact keys at a loop header are rejected for ABC/native (the budget fallback moves the hot body to the all-location key, losing the documented `BLTUI_A 50`/`ADDI_A 7` and emitting up to `budget` bodies for a win that ends around trip 36); the round-3 generic key is rejected (measured 2 extra instructions per iteration and no immediates); the dynamic join stays rejected because the static may-write pre-widening subsumes it without a fixpoint or rebuild. ARCHITECTURE now has three static canonicalization points (residual-call/module entry → all-location; non-entry loop header → loop-invariant; per-pc budget → all-location), a loop may-write fact in module facts, a "one version per loop header" invariant, per-version (not per-pc) layout wording, and three rejected alternatives with their measured costs. Q9 is revised to a native version-policy gate with the recommendation to adopt (one header version instead of two, invariant C-frame constants kept, the peel dropped); Q12 opens where per-pc layouts and may-write sets are computed; Q4/Q5/Q10/Q1 refined. Deliverables are committed as `arch_loop round 5`.

question: Round 5 fixed the loop-header key form (loop-invariant) but sketched the load-bearing may-write predicate concretely as a pc interval [header..largest backedge source] plus a CALL/TCALL argument clause. What exactly is "the loop body", and is the backedge instruction — especially a self-tail call that rebuilds the frame — part of the body or the join? (Ranked above whether may-write is a correctness condition, answered as a by-product, and above Q12's fact ownership, refined.)
evidence: experiments/6-may-write.md §2 and experiments/6-may-write.lua (artifacts 6-may-write-out/counter.dis, exit-pop.dis): on the exact documented counter (frontend/tests/optimize.lua:229), `loop` is function 2, header pc 0x29, C height 4, one self-tail `TCALL` backedge at pc 0x48, body CSETs slots 2 and 3. Round 5's interval+CALL/TCALL rule marks may-write {0,1,2,3} (0 of 4 constants kept — the generic G key), because the tail call replaces the frame and gathers arguments at C base 4-4=0; the cycle-body rule marks {2,3} (2 of 4 constants kept), which is the incumbent's measured two-unknown-slot body with `BLTUI_A 50`/`ADDI_A 7`. So round 5's own predicate makes its flagship P shape unreachable.

experiments/6-may-write.md §3: an exit-path fixture whose exit pops the frame (CGET.A 0; CPOP; CPOP; CPOP; RET) is marked {0,1,2} by the pc interval (min C height 0) and {0} by the cycle body (min C height 3). The interval contains live code that is not on a cycle through the header, so round 5's 'dead code in the interval only over-widens' is false.

experiments/6-may-write.md §4–6: exact keys are the correctness rule, so may-write is a heuristic — over-widening loses constants, under-widening only makes the backedge create another version (bounded by the per-pc budget, Q2), and every version body stays correct. The call clause is unnecessary: a callee frame starts at the caller's call-time C height (src/symbolic.c:467-484), a callee addresses only its own C frame (src/verify.c C cases), machine_return restores frame.cbase, and a residualized call does not change n[C]; caller-side pops are already caught by the min-height clause. The ABC A/B clause is vacuous because ABC keys are A/B-empty after round 3's drain.

experiments/6-gather.lua and experiments/6-gather3.lua (all four execution modes): the ABC gather is slot-identity — argument 0 is the first pushed value, callee C_k <- selected-stack depth k (`f(1,2,3)` returns `1 2 3` from CGET 0,1,2), matching docs/spec.md 'Calls' and gen/banked.lua:234. A same-function self-tail transport therefore preserves positions; a computed/re-ordered argument vector is widened at the edge (quality, not soundness).

experiments/6-may-write.md §7: a cross-function tail cycle (mutual tail calls) has no per-function cycle body and no position identity, so round 5's claim that mutual tail recursion keeps its invariant constants is unsupported — the conservative answer is the all-location key or no inlining (Q14).
decision: Q13 is answered: the loop body is the cycle body (pcs on a path from the header to a backedge source, excluding the backedge instructions), and the backedge instruction is the join, not a body write — a self-tail TCALL defines the target frame from its argument vector exactly as binding.join defines a join target. The ABC predicate is C-only: slot k is may-write iff the cycle body's min C height <= k or a CSET in the cycle body targets k; native adds A/B depth d iff min A/B height <= d. The pc interval and the CALL/TCALL clause are rejected with measured costs (interval+CALL: 0 constants kept on the documented counter; cycle body: 2 — the incumbent's shape; exit-pop: {0,1,2} vs {0}). May-write is stated as a specialization heuristic, not a correctness condition: exact keys keep any widening sound, under-widening only adds versions bounded by the per-pc budget, so no fixpoint, no completeness obligation and no cross-function analysis is needed. ARCHITECTURE now names the cycle body/backedge-as-join/transport and the heuristic status, records the rejected interval predicate with its numbers, adds backedge instructions/cycle bodies/per-pc heights/CSET targets to module facts, pins Q12's data set, and opens Q14 (cross-function tail cycles, where round 5's invariant-constant claim does not hold). Q5/Q10/Q11/Q12 are refined; deliverables committed as `arch_loop round 6`.
next: Q14 (do cross-function tail cycles keep invariants, or take the all-location key / stay residual), then Q12's ownership decision: one shared shape/cycle-body pass in the core, with the verifier's discarded Shape heights showing the data is already computed today. Q2 still blocks a single budget number and Q1 remains the scope gate.
